question.problem:
Consider the set $A,$ defined by 

$$
A=\{(x,y)\in {R}^{2}\,:\,4{x}^{2}+{y}^{2}>4\}.
$$

The boundary of $A$ is given by

$$
∂A=\{(x,y)\in {R}^{2}\,:\bbox[5px,border:1px solid black]{\phantom{AAAAA}}\,\}.
$$

What is the missing expression?
question.worked_solution:
The boundary of a set $A,$ denoted $∂A,$ is the set that contains all the boundary points of $A.$

The set $A$ and its boundary $∂A$ are shown below.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/differential/14245698/assets/b0c3e30fcb7e748a80cdf98892291599967151343efe671aca790b2528039c4c.png)

From the diagram, the boundary points of $A$ lie on the ellipse $4{x}^{2}+{y}^{2}=4.$

Therefore, 

$$
∂A=\{(x,y)\in {R}^{2}\,:\,4{x}^{2}+{y}^{2}=4\,\}.
$$
